title: Who bothers to leave a review?
hook: Start with a flat population and choose who leaves a rating.

knows: arithmetic means, rates and simple plotted values
doesNotKnow: mostly 1- and 5-star reviews, because people with moderate experiences don't post.

misconception: Treating j-shaped reviews as valid without checking the stated model, denominators or causal assumptions.
objective: mostly 1- and 5-star reviews, because people with moderate experiences don't post.
keyState: Both finite cases completed; their computed summaries retained.

claims.text: Each rating 1–5 has 20 users. All 1- and 5-star users review, but only one user at each middle rating does. What share of visible reviews is extreme?
claims.source: src/demos/probability/p100-j-shaped-reviews/spec.ts; exact finite illustration specified in manager numericCase: Experience ratings [1,2,3,4,5] each20 people. Full mean3. Select all1/5 star users and only1 each at2/3/4: 43 reviews, mean3 but extreme share40/43 instead of40/100; symmetric selection changes shape, not necessarily mean.
